documentation.title: Professional Machine Learning Engineer — Google Cloud
documentation.overview: This professional certification covers building and operating machine-learning and AI solutions on Google Cloud, from low-code modeling to production systems. Its current blueprint includes BigQuery ML and AutoML, model selection and adaptation, dataset preparation, notebook experimentation, training infrastructure, batch and online inference, pipeline automation, and production monitoring. It also includes generative-AI solution evaluation, prompt and context engineering foundations, responsible AI, and protections for data and models. The scope is organized around architecture, collaboration, scaling, serving, orchestration, and monitoring.
topics: Low-code AI with BigQuery ML, AutoML, and model APIs
Data exploration, privacy, feature handling, and notebook prototyping
Model choice, training, tuning, and compute selection
Batch and online inference, endpoint security, and serving scale
Pipeline orchestration, retraining, metadata, and lineage
AI safety, explainability, drift, and production evaluation

references.title: Professional Machine Learning Engineer Certification Exam Guide

documentation.excerpt: A Professional Machine Learning (ML) Engineer builds, evaluates, productionizes, and optimizes AI solutions using Google Cloud capabilities

documentation.title: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) - AWS Certified AI Practitioner
documentation.overview: This foundational credential focuses on recognizing AI and machine-learning concepts, choosing suitable approaches for business needs, and understanding how AWS services support AI solutions. Its AIF-C01 guide covers the AI/ML lifecycle and use cases, generative-AI capabilities and limits, foundation-model application design and evaluation, prompt engineering, responsible-AI considerations, and security, compliance, and governance. The target exam role is oriented toward using AI/ML offerings rather than building models or deploying AI infrastructure.
topics: AI/ML concepts, use cases, lifecycle, and outcome metrics
Generative AI fundamentals, model limits, business fit, and AWS infrastructure
Foundation-model selection, RAG, prompting, customization, and evaluation
Responsible AI, fairness, explainability, and transparency
AI system security, privacy, governance, and compliance
documentation.excerpt: This certification focuses on practical business applications of AI.

documentation.title: FinOps Certified Engineer
documentation.publisher: The Linux Foundation, listed on Credly
documentation.overview: FinOps Certified Engineer validates an engineering-focused grasp of cloud FinOps: making infrastructure decisions with cost and business value in view throughout the development lifecycle. The credential is aimed at engineers operating cloud infrastructure and covers practical disciplines such as efficiency, optimization, rightsizing, and tagging strategy. The Linux Foundation classifies it as an intermediate certification earned through study, activity-based learning, and a knowledge exam.
documentation.excerpt: cost-informed decisions throughout the development lifecycle

documentation.title: FinOps Certified FOCUS Analyst
documentation.publisher: The Linux Foundation, listed on Credly
documentation.overview: FinOps Certified FOCUS Analyst demonstrates practical working knowledge of the FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS). It focuses on working with FOCUS-compliant billing datasets, converting non-conformant source data into FOCUS format, and using the specification’s use-case library to answer business questions. The Linux Foundation lists it as an intermediate certification built around at least five hours of study and activity-based learning, followed by an online knowledge exam.
topics: Converting source data into FOCUS format
Applying the FOCUS Use Case Library

documentation.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
documentation.overview: This beginner-level credential tests broad familiarity with cloud computing and Azure. Its AZ-900 blueprint spans cloud models, service types, shared responsibility, and consumption-based pricing; Azure’s core architecture, compute, networking, storage, identity, and security; and the tools used for cost control, governance, deployment, and monitoring. The exam is organized into three weighted areas: cloud concepts, Azure architecture and services, and Azure management and governance. The guide reviewed here lists skills measured as of July 20, 2026.
topics: Cloud models, shared responsibility, service types, and cost models
Azure regions, resource hierarchy, compute, and networking
Storage options, migration, identity, and access controls
Security concepts, including Zero Trust and defense in depth
Cost management, policy, compliance, and resource administration
Monitoring, service health, and operational guidance tools
documentation.excerpt: You can also describe features and tools to secure, govern, and administer Azure.

documentation.title: FOCUS 1.1 Now Available. Adoption Continues for Practitioners and Vendors.
documentation.overview: Introduction to FOCUS is a free entry-level course for people who consume FinOps reports or examine billing outputs without directly manipulating cost data. The FinOps Foundation says it covers FOCUS goals, sample use cases, and gathering FOCUS-formatted datasets. It offers organization-wide orientation for leadership, finance, procurement, product, engineering, allied personas, and people who build, market, or sell FinOps tools.
topics: FOCUS orientation for FinOps report consumers
documentation.excerpt: This course covers the goals of FOCUS, sample use cases, and how to gather FOCUS-formatted datasets.

documentation.title: FinOps Certified Practitioner
documentation.publisher: The Linux Foundation, listed on Credly
documentation.overview: FinOps Certified Practitioner establishes foundational working knowledge of FinOps principles, capabilities, and practices across business, IT, and finance. It prepares learners to make evidence-based decisions about cloud use and business value, with coverage organized around the FinOps lifecycle: Inform, Optimize, and Operate. The Linux Foundation positions it for people in cloud, finance, and technology roles; earning the credential requires course participation and a knowledge exam.
documentation.excerpt: make evidence-based decisions in near-real time

documentation.title: FinOps for Containers
documentation.publisher: The Linux Foundation, listed on Credly
documentation.overview: FinOps for Containers recognizes learning focused on applying FinOps to shared container and Kubernetes environments. The Linux Foundation describes learners as able to communicate container costs with non-engineers, find wasted spend, set up cost observability, and address idle and shared resources. Its public badge also lists broad FinOps skills, while the course-specific outcomes center on visibility, attribution, and cost optimization for container workloads.
topics: Identifying wasted cost in container environments
